reason: The cited evidence (E2, E3, E4) supports laser cladding for wear resistance and the use of AlCoCrFeNi-WC for hardness/wear, but provides no data on hot cracking reduction, residual stress mitigation, or the specific 30–60% hardness improvement claim. E1 directly warns that laser cladding of HEAs can cause cracking due to thermal stress, which contradicts the crack-free premise.
premises: Laser cladding of AlCoCrFeNi HEA with WC particles yields a fine-grained, crack-free microstructure with strong metallurgical bonding.
The HEA-WC coating increases surface hardness by 30–60% over the substrate and fusion weld repairs.
The HEA-WC coating reduces wear rates compared to untreated and fusion-welded surfaces.
The HEA-WC coating reduces the incidence of hot cracking compared to traditional fusion welding.
Laser cladding mitigates hot cracking hazards by reducing residual stresses through rapid solidification.
